images.observations: South front: central five red-framed bays and six columns, three-bay wings, pale end wall strips with small windows, continuous base openings, central porch, platform open balustrade and raised approach. Three green/gold roof groups and central taller ridge remain distinct; the render does not independently measure their heights.

Southeast elevated v3 view: three connected roof volumes with pale gold decorated gables and independent wing hips; actual curved bridge void visible below the raised front platform; side upper window group, pale end wall and low arched entrance remain distinct. Source photographs support broad form and bay rhythm, while ornament patterns and all metric heights remain author estimates.

North oblique: central wall is intentionally mostly plain with horizontal bands and limited end window groups; it is not copied from the south colonnade. Low north canopy/short stair is distinct from south raised platform. Trees obscure the reference north threshold and detailed opening count, so this render supports conservative model scope rather than a measured northern restoration.

High roof view: three connected hipped-and-gabled roofs, taller central mass, separate wing ridges, gold ridge/hip outlines and curved lower eaves. Side gables remain visible at the transitions. The model omits precise survey-based tile counts, hidden joinery and faithful ornament reproduction.

Bridge close view shows a genuinely open transverse arched void with visible opposite light/ground, shaped arch soffit, solid flanking piers/deck and open balustrade gaps. The image is consistent with18 independent full-scene bidirectional centre/shoulder clear rays and deck/pier positives. It does not certify surveyed clearance or walking on the elevated deck.

West side detail: one central two-tier red-framed window group, broad pale flanks, four small base windows, genuinely recessed arched timber entrance with stone arch shoulder, small projecting balcony with open railing and separate lower stair. East upper details remain partly photo-obscured and estimated; no exact mirrored-photo claim.

South central entry detail: recessed closed timber door behind projecting canopy and slender supports; canopy-top open balustrade, tall red facade columns, real upper arched glazing, surrounding window lattice and platform/bridge rails have visible depth. Door is represented as closed, not an open-through indoor route.
